cohort: The study analyzed binge drinking data from 137,898 females aged 15-16 in the HBSC study and 267,359 in the ESPAD study, linking it to population-level fertility rates for the same cohorts when aged 16-19 across 43-45 countries/regions.
finding: The association between adolescent binge drinking and teenage fertility rates significantly diminishes when accounting for country-specific time trends, suggesting it reflects broader secular trends rather than a direct causal explanation for recent developments in teenage fertility rates.
followup_time: Up to 4 years (binge drinking at 15-16, fertility rates at 16-19)
